author: @fl0rianr

evidence.api_compatibility: No breaking changes. The thenoise display_name was simplified from "TheNoise ROCm" to "TheNoise" and a new bin_variants entry `cuda` was appended to the existing `rocm`. The version pin for thenoise was bumped from 0.10.1 to 0.12.1 for both roc and cuda entries — this is a version upgrade, not a breaking API change, but the bump should be verified against the actual thenoise-0.12.1 release. The PR declares no breaking changes and the diff confirms backward-compatible additions only.
evidence.documentation: Documentation is updated across five locations: README.md (CUDA row added to the image-generation table), docs/dev/backends-reference.md (CUDA backend tier table row and updated display name), docs/guide/cli.md (thenoise section heading updated), docs/guide/configuration/README.md (new `cuda_bin` config option documented), and src/cpp/resources/backend_versions.json (comment updated to describe the shared release asset naming convention). All doc changes are consistent with the code changes.
evidence.manual_release_testing: The commit introduces two user-visible surfaces — the `thenoise` `cuda_bin` config option (defaulting to `builtin`) and the `cuda` backend variant for the thenoise recipe — but no evidence shows a non-author exercised either end-to-end before merge. CI passed (C++ build, Launchpad PPA, llama.cpp validation all green), but CI does not run TheNoise CUDA. The author tested locally on RTX 4090/5090 but used a TheNoise fork's assets; the release-qualified asset version was not available at the time of author testing, as the PR notes a merge dependency on the next official thenoise release containing the CUDA assets.
evidence.post_approval_commits: One commit (03dc3485) was added after the first and only human approval at 2026-10-29T15:19:12Z. Its subject is 'fix(thenoise): restrict linux to x86'. It wraps the CUDA backend row in thenoise.h with `#if defined(__x86_64__)` guards, updates the install_params check from `__linux__` to `__linux__ && __x86_64__`, and tightens the error message and test preprocessor conditions accordingly. This is a narrow safety fix that prevents ARM64 or non-x86 hosts from attempting a CUDA install that would fail. It does not add new behavior, does not change the approved scope, and does not weaken tests.
evidence.review: PR #4001 received a substantive review from @bitgamma, who is listed as a maintainer with thenoise subject-area expertise. @bitgamma initially requested changes, suggesting the PR be split into two PRs (version bump and device-argument addition). The author merged those changes back into a single PR and resubmitted. @bitgamma then approved with "LGTM". The PR was also reviewed by the automated CodeRabbit bot, which flagged several issues (CUDA architecture mismatch on mixed-architecture hosts, ROCm device-index validation, GPU probe performance on every upscale call); all were marked as addressed in subsequent commits. Only one human review is present and it spans the full diff. Requested reviewers @kpoineal and @jeremyfowers did not submit reviews.
evidence.security: No security concerns. The commit adds no new network call paths, credential handling, or execution of untrusted input. It references the upstream `lemonade-sdk/thenoise` GitHub release for asset downloads, which is the established download pattern. The CUDA code path adds GPU-device-index validation and UUID-based `CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES` masking, which are hardening improvements.
evidence.tests: The author reports local testing on RTX 4090 and RTX 5090 GPUs using CUDA assets from a TheNoise fork. The diff adds a C++ unit test in test/cpp/test_runtime_config_backend_validation.cpp that calls TheNoiseServer::get_install_params("cuda", ...) on Linux x86_64 and verifies the correct archive filename, and on non-matching platforms verifies the call rejects with a runtime error. The test also adds config validation entries for `thenoise.cuda_bin`. No end-to-end test is present, which is typical for a new backend add-on.

maintainer_todos.text: Run `lemonade thenoise --backend cuda` on a Linux x86_64 host with an NVIDIA GPU and confirm the server starts, loads a model, and completes an image-generation request without error.
Set `thenoise.cuda_bin` to `builtin` and `thenoise.backend` to `cuda` in the config file, then confirm the server selects the CUDA path on startup and the thenoise recipe works.

subject: feat(backends): add TheNoise CUDA support (#4001)
summary: Adds TheNoise CUDA backend for Linux x86_64 using the portable NVIDIA bundle from the thenoise-0.12.1 release, while retaining existing ROCm support.
verdict_reason: A user-visible feature adding a new CUDA backend and a new config option was merged without evidence that a non-author manually exercised it end-to-end before release.
